correctness.rationale: For any d-dimensional polytope a vertex-only simplex triangulation and the exact affine simplex CDF give the verified coefficient d vol(T)/product of differences for every section-spline knot. For each vertex w, the rational coefficient cannot vanish identically since at directions strictly exposing w all denominators have the same negative sign; hence it is nonzero on a dense open subset of any generic sphere patch. At any exposed edge choose a direction exposing one endpoint just above the other, isolate the latter as the only knot in a common near-support interval, and vary its height continuously. The d-th distributional derivatives are nonzero atoms at pairwise distinct sites, proving linear independence and contradicting finite separated rank. All quantifiers, normalization, nonsimple vertices, dimensions d>=2, and boundary intervals are handled. Exact-rational checks in checks.py confirm square and tetrahedron instantiations; they are explicitly not relied on for the universal assertion.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is uniform infinite exact separation rank for every polytope on a common near-support interval, localized near any exposed edge. The most relevant prior theorem [arXiv:2610.10229, Theorem 4.3] assumes an infinitely smooth body in even dimension; the present polytopal theorem applies in every dimension and has a different proof mechanism. Lasserre and Shapiro provide fixed-direction spline formulas but do not assert universal noncancellation of a second-highest vertex coefficient on a nearby edge patch or the resulting common-interval infinite-rank obstruction. Exact statement/implication comparisons were made, not merely title matching. A short argument from classical spline machinery creates an acknowledged residual chance of an older unindexed equivalent result.
residual_risks: The 2014 simplex formula and older spline theory make an unindexed earlier derivation of the same infinite-rank consequence possible; no claim of priority certification.

value.rationale: The theorem completely excludes the entire class of full-dimensional convex polytopes from a natural finite-separability problem for parallel-section functions introduced in recent geometric tomography. The strong edge-local and common-interval formulation removes any regularity assumption on separated factors and identifies a geometric obstruction at every exposed edge. This is not a finite table calculation, a routine numeric improvement, or a restatement of the established fixed-direction spline formula: the noncancellation and direction-varying rank mechanism are necessary additional steps. It gives a concrete nonsmooth companion to the open boundary-separability classification while explicitly not resolving the odd-dimensional smooth problem.
